articles.title: Should I Buy ONDS? ONDS 2026 Analysis - Intellectia AI™
articles.summary: ONDS has strong near-term catalysts (DCMA Blue List certification for Optimus + FY26 revenue guidance raised to $170M–$180M) and a sharply improving Street outlook (multiple price-target hikes and broad Buy/Outperform coverage). While the tape is currently soft (bearish MACD, price below pivot), the stock is trading right on a key support area (~11.22), and options positioning is decisively call-skewed—suggesting traders are leaning bullish into the catalyst cycle. ## Analyst Ratings and Price Target Trends. Multiple firms raised price targets and reiterated Buy/Outperform (e.g., Stifel to $18, Oppenheimer to $16, Lake Street to $19, Northland to $16, H.C. Wainwright to $25). Wall Street pros: accelerating momentum/visibility, raised FY26 outlook, differentiated defense drone positioning, and perceived long runway in autonomous systems. According to Wall Street analysts, the average 1-year price target for ONDS is 12 USD with a low forecast of 10 USD and a high forecast of 17 USD. However, analyst price targets are subjective and often lag stock prices, so investors should focus on the objective reasons behind analyst rating changes, which better reflect the company's fundamentals. According to Wall Street analysts, the average 1-year price target for ONDS is 12 USD with a low forecast of 10 USD and a high forecast of 17 USD. However, analyst price targets are subjective and often lag stock prices, so investors should focus on the objective reasons behind analyst rating changes, which better reflect the company's fundamentals. Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann raised the firm's price target on Ondas to $18 from $17 and keeps a Buy rating on the shares following last week's virtual investor day to present a teach-in of their Autonomous Systems portfolio and their recently acquired businesses. While Ondas is still in the early days of executing on their business model, the company's targets were "nicely above our estimates and we gained greater appreciation of their differentiated approach to the military drone space," the analyst tells investors following the event. Oppenheimer analyst Timothy Horan raised the firm's price target on Ondas to $16 from $12 and keeps an Outperform rating on the shares. The company hosted an OAS -- Ondas Autonomous Systems -- Investor Day last week and raised 2026/30 guidance, which the firm sees as conservative.

articles.title: ONDS Stock Draws Traders After Explosive Q2 Growth
articles.summary:
## Why Traders Are Zeroing In On ONDS Momentum

The core ONDS bull case right now is simple: this is turning into a scaled defense and autonomy platform, not a small speculative drone play. Q2 2026 revenue hit a record $83.8M, up 67% sequentially and more than 13x year over year. Management then raised full‑year 2026 guidance to $525–$550M and outlined a path to adjusted EBITDA breakeven at the platform level by Q4 2026. That is hyper‑growth territory. [...] Record Q2 2026 revenue hit $83.8M, up 67% quarter over quarter and more than 13x year over year, with full‑year guidance raised to $525–$550M and backed by $1.4B in cash.
 New orders of $175M in Q2 plus $105M early in Q3 expanded the ONDS pro forma backlog to about $757M, including DZYNE and Cyberhawk programs.
 Through Mistral, ONDS landed an additional U.S. Army order above $50M for Lethal Unmanned Systems, lifting total awards on that program beyond $240M. [...] Analysts are responding. Oppenheimer raised its ONDS price target from $16 to $18 and reiterated Outperform after the Q2 beat, while other firms have highlighted upside tied to the accelerated revenue outlook. For active traders, that kind of sell‑side confirmation can become a near‑term catalyst as shorts and late bulls reposition around the new numbers.

## Conclusion

articles.title: Sticking With This Ondas Price Target as FCC Drone Update Weighs on Stock | TheStreet Pro
articles.summary:
There was news. Early last week, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission increased regulation restricting foreign-made drones and their components. In fact, the FCC released a public notice announcing that it will generally deny equipment authorizations for non-U.S. made drones and drone parts. Drones and drone parts already in the country are not impacted, but the future of foreign made equipment certainly will be. [...] Almost a month ago, I wrote to "Stocks Under $10" readers about one of my then-newer holdings, Ondas Holding  (ONDS) .

I showed readers a falling-wedge pattern of bullish reversal, slapped a target price of $11.70 on the shares and then watched from a distance. The shares were trading at a rough $9.00 at the time. They went on to peak at $9.86 (my old NYSE badge number, save the decimal) before behaving in a somewhat volatile way. [...] The histogram of the nine-day EMA is sitting right at the zero-bound. That's neither bullish nor bearish. The 12-day and 26-day EMAs are running together. Both are in positive territory, which is bullish, but if the 26-day line overtakes the 12-day line that would be bearish. I'm rooting for the 12-day EMA.

## Updated Plan for ONDS

Target Price: $11.70 (reiteration)

Upside Pivot: 21-day EMA (currently $8.50)

Downside Pivot: $7.25 (trough in the double top)

articles.summary:
Title: A Look At Ondas (ONDS) Valuation After Palantir Partnership And Defense Acquisitions
A Look At Ondas (ONDS) Valuation After Palantir Partnership And Defense Acquisitions. | Ondas Holdings  ONDS | 9.60  9.75 | 0.00%  +1.56% Pre |. Ondas (ONDS) has moved into the spotlight after announcing a partnership with Palantir and World View Enterprises, alongside acquisitions of Rotron Aerospace and Indo Earth Moving, reshaping its role in autonomous defense and critical infrastructure technologies. This suggests that investors are pricing in higher growth expectations and execution risk in equal measure. If you are looking beyond Ondas and want to see what else is gaining traction in critical infrastructure and defense technology, the 26 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks is a useful way to surface potential ideas. With Ondas now valued at about US$4.73b, trading at US$11.28 and sitting roughly 63% below the average analyst price target, the key question is whether the recent newsflow leaves upside on the table or if the market already reflects future growth. According to the most followed narrative, Ondas has a fair value of $19.50 versus the last close at $11.28, which frames the stock as meaningfully discounted and tightly linked to a specific vision for its role in autonomous defense and critical infrastructure. *The market recently caught a glimpse of this vision’s potential with the announcement of a twenty-million-dollar initial purchase order for a national autonomous border protection program. They are no longer just a company that sells hardware; they are the architects of a "Sovereign Security Grid." By integrating AI-driven command software with multi-domain hardware, they are offering a turnkey solution for protecting critical infrastructure and national borders that is automated, "always-on," and resilient against the evolving chaos of modern drone warfare.*. However, this hinges on turning the US$47.66m net loss and ambitious revenue growth assumptions into durable cash generation, while proving that large defense orders are repeatable rather than one offs. With sentiment clearly split between bold upside and execution risk, this is a moment to look at the numbers yourself and decide quickly where you stand. ## Looking for more investment ideas? If Ondas has your attention, do not stop here. Note that our analysis may not factor in the latest price-sensitive company announcements or qualitative material.
